newsitem.title: FINLAND: STOCKMANN SEES 1997 PROFIT UP ON 1996.
newsitem.headline: STOCKMANN SEES 1997 PROFIT UP ON 1996.

text.p: Finnish retailing group Oy Stockmann Ab said on Tuesday it expected full-year 1997 profit before extras to improve on last year's 315.9 million markka.

"Since the earnings trend in the first part of the year was better than anticipated, the board of directors now estimates that the 1997 profit before extraordinary items ... will be better than it was in 1996," Stockmann said in a statement with its January-June results.
"The operational result will be better than the previous estimate, exceeding last year's result," Stockmann said.
The group had earlier said it expected full-year 1997 earnings to at least match 1996.
In its H1 report, Stockmann said it expected full-year 1997 sales to top 8.0 billion markka against 7.4 billion in 1996.
First half sales rose 12.8 percent to 3.96 billion markka and Stockmann said its sales growth had outpaced the industry.
"Sales by the retail trade are forecast to develop favourably in Finland also in the latter part of 1997," Stockmann said.
